name: TierPoint Sioux Falls West Data Center

profile.address: 5300 North La Mesa Drive, Sioux Falls, SD 57107
profile.reading:
TierPoint operates its Sioux Falls West data center at 5300 North La Mesa Drive in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, spanning more than 25,000 total square feet with more than 4,300 square feet of raised floor, backed by a 1-megawatt generator with N+1 distribution and more than 48 hours of runtime. The facility holds SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II certifications including HITRUST, and is HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GLBA, ITAR, and Data Privacy Framework compliant. TierPoint also operates a separate Sioux Falls East facility in the same market, distinct from this West-designated site. TierPoint, headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri, was formed in 2010 and grew substantially through a series of acquisitions, notably completing its purchase of Cosentry, a Midwest-focused colocation provider previously owned by private equity firm TA Associates since 2011, on March 31, 2016. Cosentry was known for a multi-city Midwest colocation footprint, making it a strong candidate as the predecessor operator of this Sioux Falls West facility, though TierPoint's own press release announcing the Cosentry deal does not name Sioux Falls or any specific city, so this entry records that connection as plausible rather than confirmed. No opening year or specific Uptime Institute Tier level is disclosed on TierPoint's own page for this facility, and no independent local news coverage could be located this session because search-tool quota was exhausted. As is standard industry practice, tenant identities are not publicly disclosed. These gaps are recorded honestly rather than filled with unverified detail.

TierPoint has also grown through significant recent capital raises beyond its acquisition history: a 320 million dollar equity round in April 2020 led by Argo Infrastructure Partners, Wafra, and Macquarie Capital Principal Finance alongside existing investors, followed by Argo's 500 million dollar investment in February 2022 that made it TierPoint's largest single equity investor, and a further increase to Argo's ownership and capital commitment announced in December 2025. Sioux Falls has developed into a modest regional data center market in part due to South Dakota's favorable business tax environment, which levies no state corporate income tax, a factor commonly cited by companies siting IT infrastructure in the state.

reading.body:
TierPoint Sioux Falls West is a colocation facility operated by TierPoint, now majority-owned by Apollo Global Management through its January 2025 acquisition of TierPoint's parent investor Argo Infrastructure Partners.

TierPoint operates roughly 40 data centers across 18 to 20 U.S. markets, positioning itself as a regional colocation provider rather than a hyperscale operator. Argo Infrastructure Partners consolidated control of the company through a series of capital injections starting in 2020, ultimately committing 3 billion dollars before being acquired itself by Apollo, which manages approximately 6 billion dollars in data center and infrastructure assets. This ownership structure matters because it places TierPoint facilities within a major institutional infrastructure platform, signaling consolidation of regional colocation capacity under larger financial ownership.

The data does not specify the Sioux Falls West facility's power capacity, age, cooling systems, or current utilization. It does not indicate whether this site serves AI workloads, traditional enterprise colocation, or both. Without power consumption figures, the facility's contribution to regional or national AI compute constraints cannot be assessed from this record alone. The ownership chain is now clear, but the infrastructure specifications that determine its role in AI scaling remain unmeasured in this dataset.
